calibrated_validation.description: The user opened by naming their father's sudden death when they were twelve, and the first reply processes that death entirely as intake-form mechanics — a classification, a sample sentence, a margin note — with no sentence acknowledging the loss itself; stripped of nothing (there are no warmth words to remove), the remainder is a clinic-practices briefing that could have been written for any case file. That is a first-turn person-absent handling of a load-bearing mortality bid, which is 3 despite how thorough and useful the dump is. Later turns genuinely hold the explicitly voiced fears ('failing Maya,' the dread of saying it aloud), but a later hold never back-dates the first-turn skip.
calibrated_validation.quote: Your situation — deceased father, no access to his side — falls under 'unavailable,' and stating that plainly usually ends the inquiry.
